# `@openshell` directives

<!-- Generated by `openshell-annotate docs` from src/spec.rs. Do not edit; run `scripts/gen-docs.sh`. -->

A directive is a source comment whose text starts with `@openshell`. It must be the first thing in the comment line (after the comment leader), so prose that merely mentions `@openshell` is ignored. Unknown directives and attributes are errors, mirroring OpenShell's strict schema.

## Grammar

```ebnf
directive = "@openshell" , ws , body ;
body      = egress | provider | fs | bin | process | ignore ;
egress    = "egress" , ws , target , { ws , attr } ;
target    = host , ":" , ports ;            (* port is mandatory *)
ports     = port , { "," , port } ;
provider  = "provider" , ws , env-name , { ws , attr } ;
fs        = "fs" , ws , ( "read" | "write" ) , ws , path , { ws , attr } ;
bin       = "bin" , ws , path , { ws , attr } ;
process   = "process" , { ws , attr } ;
ignore    = "ignore" , { ws , attr } ;
attr      = key , "=" , value ;
value     = bare | '"' , { any - '"' | '\"' } , '"' ;
```

Values containing spaces must be quoted: `reason="LLM calls"`. Absolute paths may contain `=`.

## Directives

| Directive | Summary | `reason` | Lint category |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`egress`](#egress) | Allow outbound network access to a host and port(s). | required | net |
| [`provider`](#provider) | Declare that an environment variable is a credential supplied by an OpenShell provider. | optional | env |
| [`fs`](#fs) | Grant filesystem access inside the sandbox. | required | fs (write only) |
| [`bin`](#bin) | Set the binary allowed to use the egress rules in this file. | optional | exec |
| [`process`](#process) | Choose the identity the sandboxed process runs as. | optional | - |
| [`ignore`](#ignore) | Tell lint that a call site needs no policy entry (or that a denial is declined on purpose). | required | the category named by `kind` |

## Attributes accepted by every directive

| Attribute | Values | Repeatable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | `text` | no | Why this is needed. Becomes the comment above the generated entry; required where marked. |
| `scope` | `file \| next` | no | `file` makes the directive cover the whole file for lint; the default covers the call sites within `[lint] window` lines below it. |

## egress

Allow outbound network access to a host and port(s).

```
@openshell egress <host>:<port>[,<port>...] reason="..." [access=read-only|read-write|full] [protocol=rest|...] [allow="METHOD:/path"]... [bin=/path] [rule=name] [enforce=enforce|audit] [tls=skip]
```

Arguments:

- `host:port[,port...]`: Destination. A port is mandatory (OpenShell rejects endpoints without one); the host is lower-cased.

Attributes:

| Attribute | Values | Repeatable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `access` | `read-only \| read-write \| full` | no | OpenShell access preset; turns on request inspection (protocol defaults to `rest`). Mutually exclusive with `allow`. For `protocol=mcp` the preset is not written out (MCP rejects access presets); it is emitted as `mcp.allow_all_known_mcp_methods: true`. |
| `protocol` | `rest \| websocket \| graphql \| mcp \| json-rpc \| tcp` | no | L7 protocol. `tcp` is uninspected L4 and cannot be combined with `access`/`allow`/`deny`. `mcp` never emits `access`; an `access` value becomes `mcp.allow_all_known_mcp_methods: true`. |
| `enforce` | `enforce \| audit` | no | Enforcement mode for inspected endpoints (default from `[policy] enforcement`, itself defaulting to `enforce`). |
| `allow` | `METHOD:/path` | yes | Explicit allowed request, e.g. `GET:/v1/**`. Repeatable. Implies inspection. |
| `deny` | `METHOD:/path` | yes | Request subtracted from what is allowed. Repeatable; needs `allow` or `access`. |
| `bin` | `/absolute/real/path` | no | Binary that opens the connection. Overrides the nearest `@openshell bin` and `[languages]` in the config. |
| `rule` | `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` | no | Name of the `network_policies` entry (default: slug of the host). Must not start with `_provider_`. |
| `tls` | `skip` | no | Relay without TLS termination. Cannot be combined with request inspection. Use it for clients that do not trust the OpenShell CA. `openshell-prover check` reported such policies as `unsupported` with OpenShell 0.1.6 (tracked in #19). |

`reason` is required.

**Becomes:** `network_policies.<rule>.endpoints[]` (`host`, `port`/`ports`, `protocol`, `enforcement`, `access` or `rules`/`deny_rules`, or `mcp.allow_all_known_mcp_methods` for MCP) plus `binaries[]`.

## provider

Declare that an environment variable is a credential supplied by an OpenShell provider.

```
@openshell provider <ENV_VAR> [profile=<id>] [name=<instance>]
```

Arguments:

- `ENV_VAR`: Environment variable name, `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`.

Attributes:

| Attribute | Values | Repeatable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | `profile id` | no | Provider profile to use instead of the one resolved from the profile YAML's `credentials[].env_vars`. |
| `name` | `instance name` | no | Name of the provider instance to create. |

`reason` is optional.

**Becomes:** Not part of `policy.yaml`: a provider setup in the `providers.json` / `providers.sh` output (`openshell provider create ... --credential ENV`).

## fs

Grant filesystem access inside the sandbox.

```
@openshell fs read|write <absolute-path> reason="..."
```

Arguments:

- `read|write`: Access mode.
- `path`: Absolute in-sandbox path.

`reason` is required.

**Becomes:** `filesystem_policy.read_only` or `read_write` (plus `include_workdir`). Startup-only in OpenShell: it does not reload live.

## bin

Set the binary allowed to use the egress rules in this file.

```
@openshell bin <absolute-path-of-interpreter-or-binary>
```

Arguments:

- `path`: Absolute real path of the interpreter or binary inside the sandbox image (OpenShell does not follow symlinks).

`reason` is optional.

**Becomes:** `binaries[].path` of egress rules in the same file that have no `bin=`.

## process

Choose the identity the sandboxed process runs as.

```
@openshell process [user=<sandbox|uid>] [group=<sandbox|gid>]
```

Attributes:

| Attribute | Values | Repeatable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | `sandbox \| uid` | no | `process.run_as_user`. |
| `group` | `sandbox \| gid` | no | `process.run_as_group`. Conflicting values across directives are an error. |

`reason` is optional.

**Becomes:** `process.run_as_user` / `process.run_as_group`. Startup-only in OpenShell.

## ignore

Tell lint that a call site needs no policy entry (or that a denial is declined on purpose).

```
@openshell ignore kind=net|fs|env|exec|all reason="..." [scope=file]
```

Attributes:

| Attribute | Values | Repeatable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `net \| fs \| env \| exec \| all` | no | Lint category to silence (default `all`). |
| `host` | `hostname` | no | With `kind=net`: also mark denials of this host in `diff-logs` as declined. |

`reason` is required.

**Becomes:** Nothing; affects `lint` and `diff-logs` only.

## Value sets

- `protocol`: rest, websocket, graphql, mcp, json-rpc, tcp
- `access`: read-only, read-write, full
- `ignore kind`: net, fs, env, exec, all
